query: What business models and customers do these companies describe?

per_column.name: business_model_type
per_column.rationale: How a company creates and captures value (SaaS, marketplace, professional services) is a core constitutive aspect of its business profile.

per_column.name: primary_customer_segment
per_column.rationale: Who the company serves (B2B, B2C, developers, investors) is an intrinsic aspect of the business profile and directly tied to the query.

per_column.name: industry_vertical
per_column.rationale: The market/domain a company operates in is a legitimate descriptive facet of its business profile.

per_column.name: product_delivery_mode
per_column.rationale: How the offering is delivered (cloud SaaS, physical product, staffing) is an aspect of the profile, but it overlaps heavily with business_model_type (cloud_SaaS mirrors SaaS, staffing mirrors staffing_recruiting).

per_column.name: company_stage_type
per_column.rationale: Lifecycle/maturity stage is an aspect of a company's profile, though it is more about corporate maturity than the business model/customer focus of the query; still a legitimate facet.

per_column.name: core_value_proposition
per_column.rationale: The central benefit offered is a constitutive aspect of the business profile, but it substantially overlaps with industry_vertical and business_model_type (e.g., infrastructure_and_platform vs cloud_infrastructure/SaaS, financial_services vs fintech).

judge.rationale: All six columns are genuine facets (parts-of) of a company business profile rather than external predictors or causes, so the meronymy claim holds. However, mutual exclusivity is weak: product_delivery_mode is largely a projection of business_model_type (cloud_SaaS/SaaS, staffing, investment_capital all co-vary), and core_value_proposition overlaps with both industry_vertical and business_model_type (infrastructure_and_platform, financial_services, security_and_compliance restate vertical/model categories). These redundancies mean several columns capture the same underlying aspect under different names. Exhaustiveness is fairly strong: business model, customer segment, vertical, delivery mode, stage, and value proposition together cover the main constitutive aspects of the profile, well addressing the query's business-model-and-customer focus, though geographic/scale dimensions are omitted.
